Subject: Playcall: VPC upgrade — pinning strategy & rollback ladder

Team / Acme,

We're lining up the playcall for the Private (VPC) upgrade next week. High level objectives: apply the 2026-08 runtime patch, ensure version pinning for critical tenants, and validate automated rollback/evacuation across the on-prem racks. Please review and confirm any blockers below.

Proposed maintenance window: Tue 2026-08-24 00:30–03:30 PT (preference: low traffic).
Key asks for prep:
- Confirm pinning matrix (which tenants remain pinned to v2026-07 and which can move to v2026-08).
- Canary cadence: propose 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 3 phases with 15–20min observation windows.
- Rollback triggers: error-rate > 1.5% sustained for two consecutive windows, p95 latency jump > 200ms, or KV cache corruption detected.
- Network actions: will we need a brief BGP session reset for the leaf switches? (ACME ops, please advise).

Attachments: redwood_private_preflight-checklist.pdf (preflight tests + runbook snippets).

Prep items assigned: Karthik — drain/evacuation steps and KV cache draining; Laura — communication plan and SLA exceptions; Priyom — RBAC/checks and canary gating policy.

Can everyone confirm by EOD Monday so I can lock the runbook and calendar invite? If Acme needs a different window please propose.

Thanks,
Soojin

On Sun, Aug 16, 2026 at 09:12 AM Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com> wrote:
> We're lining up the playcall for the Private (VPC) upgrade next week. High level objectives: apply the 2026-08 runtime patch, ensure version pinning for critical tenants, and validate automated rollback/evacuation across the on-prem racks.

Thanks for kicking this off. A few technical clarifications and a proposed execution sequence from the runtime/ops side:

1) Rolling across racks: we'll do rack-by-rack (3 racks total), canary nodes in rack-1 (10% traffic), then expand to half of rack-2 (50%) then full rack-3 (100%). Rack boundary aligns with our vSwitch pairs; this avoids cross-rack KV consistency issues during the warmup.

2) KV cache drain: implement 2-phase drain — immediate KV-sync flush for pinned tenants, followed by background async drain for non-pinned. Drain windows per node: 90s for sync flush, 8–12 minutes for background cold-warm migration.

3) Autoscaler and schedulers: suspend autoscaling during the 10% and 50% phases to avoid noisy neighbor autoscale events. We'll re-enable after 100% stabilization.

4) Health checks & canary gates: telemetry checks include per-tenant error-rate, p50/p95 latency, token-serving throughput, and freshness of model KV cache. I'll attach the pinning-matrix.xlsx with suggested tenant-to-version mappings.

5) Rollback steps (short):
   - Step 1: mark canary nodes out of LB, switch traffic to fallback variant (v2026-07), trigger KV-cache fast-restore for pinned tenants;
   - Step 2: if post-rollback health doesn't restore within 10 minutes, trigger evacuation of the entire rack and reimage to the previous snapshot;
   - Step 3: notify CS + account team and start extended incident bridge.

I'll upload the exact shell commands and timings to the runbook link once we finalize the window.

Attachments: pinning-matrix.xlsx (suggested mapping).

-karthik
Karthik Iyer
Principal Engineer, Runtime Operations

Thanks — Acme Ops here. A couple items from our side: 

1) Window conflict: Tue 2026-08-24 00:30–03:30 PT overlaps with a large batch job we run across EU ingestion. Can we move start to 02:00 PT or shift to Wed night? We prefer minimal impact to our downstream pipelines.

2) Audit & retention: for this upgrade we need an additional 30-day fine-grained audit log retention (token-level traces + who/what API calls) for compliance. Can Redwood keep those logs in the private account for 30 days and provide a delivery URL post-maintenance?

3) E2E smoke harness: who owns the E2E automation run? We can run our acceptance tests against the canary endpoints but need the SREs to provide a short-lived credential and the expected KV state snapshot.

If we can confirm the shifted window and audit retention, Acme is OK with the canary cadence described.

Thanks everyone — quick consolidation and final decisions so we can lock the invite: 

- New maintenance window: Tue 2026-08-24 02:00–05:00 PT (per Acme request).
- Canary cadence: 10% (rack-1) -> 50% (partial rack-2) -> 100% (rack-3). Observation windows: 20m / 20m / 30m.
- Confirmed rollback triggers: sustained error-rate > 2.0% across tenant set for two consecutive observation windows, p95 latency increase > 250ms, or KV cache restore failures. These are slightly tightened vs initial ask to match Acme SLOs.
- Audit retention: Redwood will retain fine-grained audit traces for 30 days in Acme's private storage bucket and provide a signed URL post-maintenance. (Action item: Priyom to create the signed URL and ACLs).
- E2E harness: Acme will run acceptance tests against the canary endpoints; SRE will provision a short-lived IAM API token and the KV snapshot reference. (Action item: Karthik to push snapshot tag 'acme-preflight-20260824' and short-lived creds into the runbook).

- Incident contact list: +1 555-212-0099 (Soojin), +1 555-210-1122 (Karthik), +1 555-300-4455 (Acme On-call)
